keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has nothing before 3400 BCE). The phase table gives Ubaid 0 (Oueili phase) 6500-5900 BC and Ubaid 1 (Eridu style) 5900-5200 BC at "Eridu and 'Oueili in the south"; the radius around Uruk covers Eridu (24 km south-south-west of Ur, Eridu page), Ur, 'Oueili and Uruk. The Eridu page dates the city's founding c. 5400 BC (infobox 5500-5300 BC) against the Ubaid page's Ubaid 1 "Eridu style" from 5900 BC; the earlier page is followed. No area figure exists to compare.

Phase table (after Pournelle 2003): Ubaid 2 "Halaf-Ubaid Transitional" 5200-5100, Ubaid 3 "Northern Ubaid" 5100-4900, Ubaid 4 4900-4350 (after Harris 2021: Northern Ubaid 5200-4600); text: "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC", "a range of 5300-4300 BC has been suggested" for Syria. The Halaf is drawn to 5100 BCE by halaf-culture, so the north is the Ubaid's from that year. The middle Tigris around Samarra is subtracted until 4800 BCE (samarra-culture, "roughly dated to between 5500 and 4800 BCE"); about 14 cells of the Samarra culture's As Sulaymaniyah circle lie inside the Assyria region and stay in the shape (a region boundary, not a claim). Mersin, Norsuntepe, Arslantepe and Tepe Ghabristan are outlying find spots and are not drawn.

The infobox runs to 3800 BC; the keyframe stops at 4000 BCE where the Uruk-period dossier begins. The Gulf coast (Kuwait City 80 km, Al Jubayl 100 km) stays to the end: the page says Gulf Ubaid pottery peaked "around 5300 BC and continuing into the fifth millennium" and gives no end, while the southern Ubaid "spans from about 5500 to 3800 BC"; it is lost to nobody in 4000 BCE (confidence 1).

ledger.note: 6000 BCE: the Ubaid farmers of Eridu and 'Oueili, the first settlers of southern Iraq, open the map. "no archaeological site in southern Iraq has yielded remains more ancient than Ubaid"; Ubaid 0 began c. 6500 BC, before the project's first year, so the culture is drawn from 6000 BCE. The Eridu page dates Eridu's founding c. 5400 BC.

region.text: the whole southern alluvium and the Gulf coast

ledger.note: 5500 BCE: the Ubaid spreads over the whole southern alluvium and down the Gulf. "In the south the Ubaid period spans from about 5500 to 3800 BC"; "Ubaid pottery began to appear along the Persian Gulf coast toward the end of the sixth millennium BC, reaching a peak around 5300 BC". The year is the page's; the extent is this dossier's reading.

region.text: northern Mesopotamia and the Amuq: "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC"; "There are now Ubaid sites in the Amuq Valley in the northwest"

ledger.note: 5100 BCE: the northern Ubaid replaces the Halaf. Phase table (after Pournelle 2003): Ubaid 2 "Halaf-Ubaid Transitional" 5200-5100 and Ubaid 3 "Northern Ubaid" 5100-4900 (after Harris 2021: Northern Ubaid 5200-4600); the text says "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC". The Halaf infobox ends the Halaf in 5100 BC and halaf-culture dissolves in 5100 BCE, so the gain is placed where the Halaf ends; the text's 5300 BC is the start of the transition, drawn as Halaf. The year is the phase table's, the extent is this dossier's reading.

region.text: the middle Tigris around Samarra and Tell es-Sawwan

ledger.note: 4800 BCE: the Samarra culture of the middle Tigris ends and its land is Ubaid. The Ubaid page does not date the middle Tigris; the year is the Samarra page's end ("roughly dated to between 5500 and 4800 BCE", "the precursor to the Mesopotamian culture of the Ubaid period"). The Tell es-Sawwan page calls the site "a primarily Ubaid, Hassuna, and Samarra culture occupation" and the infobox says "5th millennium BC", with no level dates and no word on the middle Tigris after the Samarra culture; the year stays the Samarra page's end (confidence 1).

region.text: northern Mesopotamia and the Amuq: "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC"; "There are now Ubaid sites in the Amuq Valley in the northwest"

ledger.note: 4300 BCE: the north passes to the Late Chalcolithic. "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC" and is "succeeded by the Late Chalcolithic period", which no dossier draws; the land goes to nobody.

region.text: the Samarra circle outside the southern alluvium (the Samarra culture's land, which the Ubaid takes in 4800 BCE)

ledger.note: 4300 BCE: the middle Tigris around Samarra leaves the Ubaid with the north. "In Northern Mesopotamia the period runs only from about 5300 to 4300 BC" and is "succeeded by the Late Chalcolithic period"; the page names neither the middle Tigris nor Samarra, so counting it with the north is this dossier's placement. The Samarra circle inside the southern alluvium (about 29 cells) stays with the alluvium.

region.text: Susiana: "Susa I (terminal Ubaid) necropolis at Susa east of the Tigris"

ledger.note: 4300 BCE: terminal Ubaid at Susa. "Susa I (terminal Ubaid) necropolis at Susa east of the Tigris"; the page gives no year for Susiana, so the gain is placed at the start of Ubaid 5 (4350-4200 BC after Pournelle 2003). The Susa page dates the earliest settlement "Susa I period (c. 4200-3900 BC)", infobox "Built: 4395-4200 BCE", and says the earliest painted vessels are "a late, regional version of the Mesopotamian Ubaid ceramic tradition"; it does not date Ubaid Susiana as a whole, so the gain keeps confidence 1.

region.text: the Gulf coast: "Bahra 1 and H3 in Kuwait, Dosariyah in Saudi Arabia"

ledger.note: 4000 BCE: the Gulf coast (Kuwait, Al Jubayl) leaves the Ubaid with the end of the period. "Ubaid pottery began to appear along the Persian Gulf coast toward the end of the sixth millennium BC, reaching a peak around 5300 BC and continuing into the fifth millennium"; the page gives no end for the Gulf pottery and the southern Ubaid "spans from about 5500 to 3800 BC", so the coast is kept to the 4000 BCE end and goes to nobody (the Uruk dossier does not draw it); confidence 1, page silent.

Susiana: "Susa I (terminal Ubaid) necropolis at Susa east of the Tigris"

ledger.note: 4000 BCE: the Uruk period begins in the south. The Ubaid is "succeeded by the Uruk period"; the infobox end (c. 3800 BC) and the Uruk infobox start (c. 4000 BC) differ by two centuries and the phase table ends Ubaid 5 at 4200 BC; the handover is placed at 4000 BCE.

certainty.note: An archaeological culture, not a state: every edge is the spread of ceramic finds, never a frontier; the Gulf shore is the only hard line.

notes:
Culture dossier (type culture, Cliopatria has nothing before 3400 BCE). Project floor: Ubaid 0 began c. 6500 BC, the dossier starts at 6000 BCE. Disagreements: Ubaid end 3800 BC (infobox) vs 4200 BC (phase table) vs Uruk start 4000 BC (Uruk page), settled at 4000 BCE; north Ubaid start 5300 BC (text) vs 5100 BC (Pournelle phase table: Northern Ubaid) vs Halaf end 5100 BC (Halaf infobox; settled at 5100, see the repair note); Eridu founded 5400 BC (Eridu page) vs Ubaid 1 "Eridu style" from 5900 BC. Gazetteer: Eridu, Tell al-'Ubaid, 'Oueili, Dosariyah are not places in the gazetteer; the Uruk, Kuwait City and Al Jubayl radii stand in for them. Outlying find spots (Mersin, Norşuntepe, Arslantepe, Tepe Ghabristan, Dalma Island) are not drawn. The Late Chalcolithic of the north (4300-3800 BCE) has no dossier and is nobody's land until the Uruk expansion.

Repair 2026-10-18 (after the reviewer): (1) The northern gain from halaf-culture moves from 5300 to 5100 BCE (confidence 2), citing the phase table (Pournelle 2003: Ubaid 2 'Halaf-Ubaid Transitional' 5200-5100, Ubaid 3 'Northern Ubaid' 5100-4900; Harris 2021 gives 5200-4600) and the Halaf's own end in 5100, so the 473 cells no longer sit in two dossiers for 200 years; keyframe 1 now ends 5101 BCE and the new keyframe ubaid-period_-5100 starts the north. The text's 'about 5300 to 4300 BC' is the Transitional start, which halaf-culture draws as Halaf; I disagree with nobody here but keep the text's 5300 in the notes because the page contradicts itself (text 5300, table 5100 or 5200). (2) Keyframe 2 no longer draws the Samarra culture's land on the middle Tigris (Samarra 110 km) before 4800 BCE: it is subtracted from the northern part only (the Samarra circle inside the Babylonia region, about 29 cells, was Ubaid land from 5500 BCE in keyframe 1 and stays); a new keyframe ubaid-period_-4800 adds Samarra 110 km with the ledger gain of 4800 BCE, which now has its 148 cells in a keyframe. About 14 cells of samarra-culture's As Sulaymaniyah circle (11 in Assyria, 3 in Babylonia) remain inside this dossier's regions 5500..4800: a boundary artifact of the historical regions, not drawn on purpose. (samarra-culture, verdict pass and untouched, hands both circles to the Ubaid in 4800 although the Ubaid gains only Samarra 110 km; the As Sulaymaniyah circle is nobody's from 4800 on the Ubaid side.) (3) At 4300 BCE the Samarra circle outside the alluvium leaves with the north (new loss to nobody, confidence 1, page silent on the middle Tigris; the Tell es-Sawwan page gives no Ubaid level dates). (4) The Gulf coast (Kuwait City 80 km, Al Jubayl 100 km) is kept in keyframe 3 to 4000 BCE and lost to nobody in 4000 BCE (new event, confidence 1): the Ubaid page gives the Gulf pottery a peak at 5300 and 'continuing into the fifth millennium' with no end, and the southern Ubaid 'spans from about 5500 to 3800 BC', so the dossier's own end is the least invented year; uruk-period does not draw the coast. Pages re-read: Ubaid period, Tell es-Sawwan, Susa. Susiana (ledger 4300) stays confidence 1: the Susa page dates the settlement 'c. 4200-3900 BC' (infobox 'Built: 4395-4200 BCE') and calls its first painted ware a regional Ubaid version, which supports Ubaid influence there but not the year.
